A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HAX and joint-recall research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original joint-recall experiments, continual-pretraining results, long-context evaluations, and supplementary short-context evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: HAX retains the same LSH and key-selection components, pairwise ranking loss, combined sparse mask, and gated integration with SSMs. Added citations and equation regrouping do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same joint-recall data, language-training corpora, Ruler settings, LongBench tasks, and short-context benchmarks. The 4K extrapolation evaluation moved from v2 Appendix E.1 to v3 Section 5.2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every matched experiment, including the doubled-width SSM and Samba joint-recall baselines and the sparse-attention variants. Newly cited sparse-attention methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and testing procedures are retained. The hidden sizes, layer counts, sparsity budgets, and component allocations emphasized in v3 Section 5 were already documented in v2 Appendix D.

E4.justification: Both retain the component comparisons, context-length extrapolation test, short-context retention evaluation, and attention-pattern case study. Moving the extrapolation analysis into the main text adds no new robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both report three random seeds per learning rate for joint recall and average performance at the best-performing learning rate. Neither adds uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or a revised statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All five tables retain identical numerical entries after matching v2 Tables 1–3 to v3 Tables 2, 3, and 1; Tables 4–5 also match. The validation-loss plot and attention heatmap use identical image data.

T1.justification: The definitions, Corollary 3.1, Propositions 3.2–3.3, and Appendix A–C derivations and proofs are retained. Combining query/key equations and renumbering subsequent equations changes presentation only.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint recall, SSM expressiveness limitations, CDSA's theoretical advantage, and HAX's empirical benefits.

C2.justification: The explanations of LSH limitations, LSH/KS complementarity, training stability, and context extrapolation remain unchanged in substance. The extrapolation interpretation in v3 Section 5.2 already appeared in v2 Appendix E.1.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit HAX code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract. Implementation settings are retained, although explicit Mamba-Chat and Flash-Linear-Attention repository URLs disappear from the references.

R1.justification: New Section 6.3 expands sparse-attention context through HashAttention, Sparse Attention with Learning to Hash, Sparse Flash Attention, and Native Sparse Attention. Sparse Modular Activation and B'MOJO are also added to the hybrid-architecture discussion, without redefining the paper's contribution.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording edits, adopts numbered citations, adds equal-contribution and acknowledgement text, and reorganizes some experimental description. Most prose and the overall scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column layout, extensively changing text flow, display sizes, and float placement. The joint-recall table is reordered, the 4K table moves into the main text, captions are refined, and Figure 8 is redrawn as vector graphics.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a documented route to HAX code, broadens relevant sparse-attention context, and makes existing settings and extrapolation evidence more accessible in Section 5. These modest benefits outweigh the loss of explicit URLs for two cited implementations. The unchanged methods, proofs, and empirical evidence limit the improvement's scope.
